audits.title: Audit of antibiotic prophylaxis for surgical patients in three hospital trusts in Tayside. Tayside Area Clinical Audit Commitee.
audits.standard: Previously agreed standards for administration of antibiotic prophylaxis (three general standards)
audits.setting: Angus, Dundee Teaching Hospitals and Perth & Kinross Trusts, Tayside

cycle1.result: Prophylaxis given to 82% of eligible orthopaedic patients; rate for indicated operations 84% to 93% across trusts; continued <24 h in 78% to 97%; given within two hours in >95%; second doses in 5/44 (11%) of operations >2 h.

audits.other_findings: Trust comparison confined to six common procedures (166 operations) because results were sensitive to case mix.
audits.citation: Davey P, Napier A, McMillan J, Ruta D. Audit of antibiotic prophylaxis for surgical patients in three hospital trusts in Tayside. Tayside Area Clinical Audit Commitee. Health Bull (Edinb). 1999;57(2):118-127. PMID: 12828137.

audits.title: Change the habit to change the practice: Do audits really ever change anything?
audits.standard: Local MRSA guidelines: eradication therapy and correct induction antibiotics for MRSA-unknown patients
audits.setting: Royal Liverpool Hospital, UK major trauma centre, emergency hip fracture surgery

cycle1.result: Eradication therapy prescribed 1%; correct antibiotic choice 18%. Operation median 24.05 h from admission but MRSA swab results at median 48 h.

audits.intervention: Posters on induction antibiotics in anaesthetic rooms and stickers on MRSA eradication therapy on nursing care bundles.

cycle2.result: Eradication therapy prescribed 8%; correct antibiotic choice 94%.

audits.other_findings: Eradication therapy compliance stayed poor despite stickers.
audits.citation: Bodansky D, Oskrochi Y, Judah G, Lewis M, Fischer B, Narayan B. Change the habit to change the practice: Do audits really ever change anything?. Injury. 2017;48(9):1999-2002. doi:10.1016/j.injury.2017.04.036. PMID: 28442206.

audits.title: Identifying targets for improvement using a nationally standardized survey: Surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis in orthopedic surgery.
audits.standard: Surgical NAPS appropriateness assessment of surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis
audits.setting: 140 Australian facilities contributing Surgical National Antimicrobial Prescribing Survey audits

cycle1.result: Overall appropriateness 58.0% of 6709 doses; procedural 64.7%, postprocedural 48.3%

audits.other_findings: Commonest reasons for inappropriateness were timing of procedural doses (50.9%) and duration of postprocedural prescriptions (49.8%).
audits.citation: Ierano CE, Thursky K, Marshall C, Koning S, James R, Johnson S, et al.. Identifying targets for improvement using a nationally standardized survey: Surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis in orthopedic surgery. Infect Control Hosp Epidemiol. 2020;41(12):1419-1428. doi:10.1017/ice.2020.320. PMID: 32838821.

audits.title: Compliance with antibiotic prophylaxis guidelines in surgery: Results of a targeted audit in a large-scale region-based French hospital network.
audits.standard: French national antibiotic prophylaxis guidelines (use, agent, timing within 60 minutes before incision, initial dose, additional doses)
audits.setting: 26 public and private healthcare facilities in the Pays de la Loire regional network

cycle1.result: Overall antibiotic prophylaxis compliance 64%; correct agent 93%; correct initial dose 97.4%; given within 60 minutes before incision in 77.6%.

audits.other_findings: Seven procedures audited including total hip arthroplasty; in 26% of appendicectomies prophylaxis was given after incision. An action plan and updated regional protocol were planned.
audits.citation: Prévost N, Gaultier A, Birgand G, Mocquard J, Terrien N, Rochais E, et al.. Compliance with antibiotic prophylaxis guidelines in surgery: Results of a targeted audit in a large-scale region-based French hospital network. Infect Dis Now. 2021;51(2):170-178. doi:10.1016/j.medmal.2020.10.005. PMID: 33068683.

audits.title: Perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis in spinal surgery.
audits.standard: North American Spine Society (NASS) 2013 guideline on perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis: preoperative dose, redosing as needed, discontinuation within 24 hours for uncomplicated non-instrumented surgery
audits.setting: Spine Unit, Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery Department, Assiut University Hospitals (tertiary spine centre)

cycle1.result: All patients received a correct preoperative first-generation cephalosporin dose, but IV antibiotics continued 1–6 days followed by oral antibiotics until suture removal (up to two weeks) in all patients, with mixed agents; SSI 1 case (1.85%).

audits.intervention: New local surgical antibiotic prophylaxis protocol (first-generation cephalosporin 30–60 minutes before incision, redose after 3 hours, stop at 24 hours) agreed in discussion sessions and disseminated by pamphlet and theatre poster.

cycle2.result: All patients received preoperative first-generation cephalosporin continued for only 24 hours postoperatively and were discharged on day 2; no SSI.

audits.other_findings: Difference in infection rates was not statistically significant; mean postoperative stay fell from 3.33 to 2.04 days.
audits.citation: Shawky Abdelgawaad A, El Sadik MHM, Hassan KM, El-Sharkawi M. Perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis in spinal surgery. SICOT J. 2021;7:31. doi:10.1051/sicotj/2021029. PMID: 33973847.

audits.title: A Clinical Audit of Perioperative Antibiotic Prophylaxis and Intraoperative Monitoring in Orthopaedic Trauma Surgery: An Audit Cycle.
audits.standard: Northern Care Alliance 2023 orthopaedic antibiotic prophylaxis guideline (choice, timing within 60 minutes, duration) and NICE NG180 (blood pressure within 20% of baseline, core temperature 36.5-37.5°C); 100% target for timing and blood pressure
audits.setting: Trauma orthopaedic unit, Salford Care Organisation (Northern Care Alliance NHS hospital); adult trauma surgery

cycle1.result: Correct intraoperative antibiotic 68/104 (65.4%); given within 60 minutes 104/104 (100%); postoperative duration compliant 67/104 (64.4%); overuse 25/104 (24%); blood pressure within target 104/104 (100%); temperature documented 36/104 (35%).

audits.intervention: Planned: EPR alerts for antibiotic choice and duration, mandatory temperature documentation fields, staff education and a compliance dashboard; re-audit planned in six months.
audits.other_findings: Postoperative compliance was lowest in joint replacement (40%, overuse 37%) and best in internal fixation (75%); all documented temperatures were normothermic.
audits.citation: Khan A, Elmadbouh S, Khalid SA. A Clinical Audit of Perioperative Antibiotic Prophylaxis and Intraoperative Monitoring in Orthopaedic Trauma Surgery: An Audit Cycle. Cureus. 2025;17(6):e87082. doi:10.7759/cureus.87082. PMID: 40755948.

audits.title: Compliance With Antibiotic Prophylaxis in Hip Arthroplasty Following Neck of Femur Fractures: A Retrospective Clinical Audit Study.
audits.standard: Trust guideline: three postoperative IV doses of flucloxacillin (teicoplanin if penicillin allergic) after hip arthroplasty for NOF fracture; target 100%
audits.setting: Birmingham Heartlands Hospital, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Postoperative antibiotics given to 150/179 (83.8%), none to 29 (16.2%); 84/121 (69.4%) flucloxacillin recipients completed all three doses; 97/179 (54.2%) fully compliant overall.

audits.other_findings: Of 29 with no antibiotics, 12 were mentioned in notes but not prescribed, 8 recorded as not required and 9 not mentioned. Three superficial wound infections (1.7%) and no PJI.
audits.citation: Mersal M, Thomas J, Shahab M, Shrivastava N, Elgendy M, Embaby O, et al.. Compliance With Antibiotic Prophylaxis in Hip Arthroplasty Following Neck of Femur Fractures: A Retrospective Clinical Audit Study. Cureus. 2025;17(11):e97941. doi:10.7759/cureus.97941. PMID: 41466947.

audits.title: Audit of timing of antibiotic prophylaxis in hip and knee arthroplasty.
audits.standard: Antibiotic prophylaxis at induction of anaesthesia and at 6 and 12 h post-operatively
audits.setting: Cardiff Royal Infirmary, elective hip and knee arthroplasty

cycle1.result: All 16 received prophylaxis, but dose intervals were longer than the standard in 50% of patients for the second dose and 81% for the third dose.

audits.intervention: Practice reviewed to ensure all patients receive antibiotics at the appropriate times (details not reported).
audits.citation: Lewis K. Audit of timing of antibiotic prophylaxis in hip and knee arthroplasty. J R Coll Surg Edinb. 1998;43(5):339-340. PMID: 9803108.
